data.turoyo: Bu Sayfo nquwwolle ad dəkoṯo lə ḥḏoḏe, xrəmiwonne. Nəfqiwo bi xaṣrayo, uzzənwo bayo. <...>
data.translation: In the Sayfo they had bored through the places to one another, they used to pierce them through. They would emerge on this side, go through that one. <...>

rationale: First provisional Infectum-wa box; connected places and repeated emergence supply an understandable perforation context. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; analysis rests on the Turoyo.

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: E, kətwobən 3-4 ǧandərma. Yatiwi qume w xrəmme.
data.translation: Father Brahim: There were three or four gendarmes. They sat in front of him and riddled him with bullets.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: a compact independent human-patient context; the supplied English’s weapon specification remains explicitly qualified. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; analysis rests on the Turoyo.

summary: The one token confirms stem I Preterit xrəmle and sense 1 durchschlagen, durchbohren. The sword is an overt zero-marked patient; the awl and striking action are supplied by the preceding clause.
The result is perforation of the sword, not simply a blow against it. The occurrence adds no separate sense, stem, form box or idiom.
The entire sequence and reference 95/79 already exist. The only proposed entry change is a source-backed translation typo correction, with no duplicate example.
xrəmme with the preceding three or four gendarmes is agentive Preterit; no Detransitive follows from the person undergoing the event.
xrəmiwonne provisionally supplies Infectum-wa with a plural patient suffix and repeated going/emerging in the continuation. The exact suffix series is stronger evidence than the English tense.
The round-1 translation typo correction is retained through the previous entry and is not proposed again. No new idiom is established.
